Helios is an internal development codename managed by SHS designating the complete software and hardware framework for the EN9100 solid-state drive product line. It serves as the official internal identifier for the underlying hardware architecture, SSD controller development, wear leveling framework, firmware subsystem, Flash Translation Layer (FTL) features, and storage management operations including trim and garbage collection.

The current mature iteration implements a DRAM-less firmware architecture leveraging Host Memory Buffer (HMB) for logical-to-physical caching, with critical data integrity subsystems including the Read-Disturb Refresh Manager. It features specialized FTL and HMB lifecycle management, along with health telemetry and SMART/Health logging functions for datacenter integration.

Historical development reveals significant architectural evolution. Earlier iterations used single DRAM cache architecture with LRU eviction policy and dirty journal replay for recovery. Predecessor designs implemented only static wear leveling without dynamic allocation or disturbance handling, while reference architectures deferred wear leveling block allocation to external allocators. Prior garbage collection relied on single pool cost-benefit victim selection (later superseded by Apollo GC system). Firmware versions include 0.9.3, 0.9.4, and 0.9.6; build helios-0.9.4-rc2 underwent platform validation. Version 0.9.6 required telemetry recalibration. Helios has been used in garbage collection victim selection validation tests and datacenter SSD product validation.

Aurora is an internal development and product codename for the EN9100 enterprise solid-state drive's NVMe controller platform, engineered by SHS Semiconductor. It designates the foundational hardware architecture centered on the A0 silicon system-on-chip, serving as the primary development and bring-up target. The SoC integrates a PCIe Gen5 x4 host interface, NVMe 2.0 protocol support, an eight-channel NAND backend, and multiple firmware processing cores.

The Aurora controller platform encompasses comprehensive technical capabilities including weighted round-robin submission queue arbitration with doorbell logic, NVMe admin queue operations, namespace management, Single Root I/O Virtualization (multi-PF), power state management, Common Memory Buffer, Persistent Memory Region, asynchronous event notifications, MSI-X interrupt coalescing, end-to-end CRC with Protection Information, out-of-band management, adaptive program-suspend logic, EN9100 RTL NAND channel sequencer, inline media encryption (AES-256-XTS per-sector engine), and TCG Opal 2.0 compliance with integrated thermal control and error correction.

Throughout its lifecycle, Aurora functions as the codename for RTL hardware design, firmware targets, and test platforms across multiple engineering and validation domains—including the Helios Flash Translation Layer, DRAM operations, host interface validation, and performance tuning initiatives (sequential write optimization, PCIe lane margining, garbage collection QoS, latency monitoring). The designation applies to the product family, development boards, and analysis frameworks used for engineering task tracking, reliability assessment, and firmware verification.

The Aurora codename also designates distinct technical frameworks: one refers to an alternative single-pass decoding approach without iterative updates, while another describes a design architecture featuring a single slot, hint-based next-accept signaling during busy periods, absent suspend/resume functionality, and no plane broadcast capability.

The EN9100 is an enterprise-grade NVMe SSD and controller platform developed by SHS Semiconductor, designed for high-throughput datacenter deployments and benchmarking. It is a fifth-generation storage device built on the Aurora System-on-Chip, featuring a PCIe Gen5 x4 interface, NVMe 2.0 protocol support, and an eight-channel NAND backend with the Helios Flash Translation Layer and dedicated logical-to-physical mapping subsystem. The EN9100 employs a DRAM-less FTL v2 implementation managed via Host Memory Buffer caching with configurable over-provisioning for write amplification optimization, supporting ZNS features and power-loss protection for host-acknowledged writes.

Technically, it advances beyond legacy single-DRAM and journal-based recovery architectures through rigorous optimization of garbage collection, stream write allocation, wear leveling, 3D TLC/QLC NAND retention, raw bit error rates, read disturb characteristics, and DRAM timing, bandwidth, and ECC metrics. Development involves weekly firmware meetings, sprint-based tuning, cross-team coordination for requirement tracking, and QLC feasibility documentation. The device is validated for Gen5 throughput and P99 QoS budgets and benchmarked against specifications like Borealis; it is also supported by Aurora and Nova platforms.

Compliance mandates include cryptographic datapath standards, XTS-AES decryption data integrity, and Open Compute Project specifications. Mass-production preparation and reliability validation are gated against security and quality metrics. The EN9100 is interchangeably referenced via its Aurora codename, particularly for power droop telemetry monitoring; however, certain production iterations have experienced sudden power-off-induced metadata corruption, indicating ongoing stabilization efforts.
